📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #8. Posted per window-expiry (last notified 2026-07-11T11:20:00Z, ~45h ago, past the 24h suppression window).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Re-query p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over the monitor's own window plus a wider surrounding window — expect values in the 0.001-0.2s range. Confirm 0 error logs on service:notifications. This KB explicitly says: if a future occurrence ever shows a genuine elevated p95, treat as a break from the noise pattern and escalate immediately rather than assuming noise.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on file yet

⚠️ Note: this occurrence DID reproduce an elevated value (see below) — breaks from the "cleanest non-reproduction pattern" this entry documented for its first 7 occurrences. Flagging per the KB's own playbook step 4.

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327 ("[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high", fired 2026-07-13T08:43:07Z — synthetic degraded-cycle DD-scan candidate, no Slack MCP read path this session)

Root-cause analysis:
  • DD metric p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over 2026-07-13T08:13:07Z-08:53:07Z (240 datapoints): baseline ~0.0005-0.02s throughout, EXCEPT one outlier of 1578.86s at 08:30:00Z — far larger than any prior documented occurrence (previous max was 34.73s on a sibling low-traffic monitor family). service:notifications status:error env:prod returned 0 hits for the same window.
  • Same single-request-dominates-percentile mechanism as prior occurrences, but the magnitude here suggests a genuinely hung request or a trace-instrumentation artifact, not ordinary statistical noise. Recommend a trace-level look rather than dismissing as routine.

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
  • DD metric (1578.86s outlier): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Anotifications&exp_agg=p95&start=1783930387&end=1783932787
  • DD logs (0 errors): service:notifications status:error env:prod
  • Kibana: n/a — not the evidence datasource for this KB (evidence_source: datadog_apm)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-gateway-4xx-spike-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #8. Posted per window-expiry (last notified 2026-07-11T11:20:00Z, ~47h ago, past the 24h suppression window).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: Confirm shape — single/few adjacent 15-20s buckets carrying most of the 4xx count, immediate return to baseline. Check ms-authentication-api and Redis JWT-cache health in the same window (most plausible mechanism for a brief 4xx burst). If a future occurrence shows longer duration or correlates with 5xx/real user reports, escalate immediately — this monitor guards the single point of failure for the whole platform.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on file yet

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299544656 ("[Admin][Gateway][P3] 4xx spike (gateway)", fired 2026-07-13T10:32:56Z — synthetic degraded-cycle DD-scan candidate, no Slack MCP read path this session)

Root-cause analysis:
  • DD metric sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits.by_http_status{service:gateway,env:prod,http.status_class:4xx}.as_count() over 2026-07-13T10:17:56Z-10:32:56Z: 16 datapoints, max 3.0 — nowhere near the monitor's own >2000/15min threshold. Confirms a state-transition/sensitivity artifact, not a real breach.

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299544656
  • DD metric (max 3 vs 2000 threshold): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.hits.by_http_status&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Agateway&exp_agg=sum&start=1783938676&end=1783939576
